what: First adversarial review of pull request 3 of BRIEF-canon.md (Safe passenger on by default, covering the landing and the drag; item 5). Two lenses, as RUN-canon.md sets them: physics and claims (the landing's split, its momentum real and its energy taken back, and the drag); code, layout and the migration (the save mark, old saves with Safe passenger off, the powers-off identity, mutants, the page as rendered). Reviewed at 95a22f9 (the build) and 58c5374 (the STATUS commit on top). Each finding was reproduced or refuted by a skeptic with its own script: 8 findings, 7 confirmed (physics-catch-heat-unharmed and code-1 are the same defect, fixed once and recorded under both), 1 refuted (physics-feel-vs-no-stress, no change). Fixed as the session lead decided: decision 6 on the Catch tab (the miss callout, the palm tile and the Game of catch card, by the Throw tab's 1,200 K rule); the landing's momentum kept real and whole, and past what the ground bears over the person's facing area (about 100 m/s on the default slab; per ground in README decision 4) the page says the ground gives way where they land instead of 'no crater'; no 'quake' in the impact line; a person who hits the ground with no air in the game of catch is a Safe passenger landing (below 100% the fireball reading stays); the skeptics' fixes for the squash sentence and the drag checks. Each fix's check was seen failing with the fix reverted in a scratch copy (scratchpad pr3/r1fix/revert.py, 14 reverts), and the build's six mutants, rebuilt on the fixed tree, each still fail a check (the drag: powers.js and presence.js; the landing energy and the landing momentum: powers.js and the page; the landing blast: powers.js; the migration and a mark-2 save read as a choice: the page). After the fixes, the full test line, one test at a time: calibration 117 checks, all passed; presence 383 checks, all passed; shots 81 ok lines, 0 problems (1280 and 390 px, light and dark), its powers-off page comparison unchanged (16 states the same as main's page); powers 160/160 (both powers-off passes of 15,541 cases: the 15,533 without Safe passenger byte-identical, the 8 with it identical through part 1's shim); ladder 562/562; sweep 7,776 contexts, 0 problems. The new texts' states also checked at 390 px, light and dark: no sideways scroll, broken text or page error.
script: workflow canon-review (args {pr: 3, round: 1, lenses: [physics, code]}); kept in history at the end of the run

verified_ok: The brief's and the README's least-effort figures, from my own engine script at 3,000 kg, four powers and Safe passenger on, default dial: least disruptive 3,342 kg-force (3.68%). It releases at 16.44 m/s, goes 30.05 m and lands at 18.01 m/s, like a 16.53 m fall (v²/2g). Eimpact is 14,634 J (½mv² = 14,638 J), and the momentum to the ground is 1,625 kg·m/s.

The landing pulse: L = 0.5594 m (sphere of 90.26 kg at 985 kg/m³), T = L/v = 31.06 ms, mean 59.1 g, peak 118 g (Hann). The pulse is byte-identical with the switch off (landShake), so the ground shakes 'as a real landing does', and ls.F·T/2 equals the momentum.

The landing's split (momentum real, energy taken back) fits canon. A landing is not on canon's momentum list, so its momentum must reach the ground, and absorbing the energy is allowed. The quick stop is better justified than the README says. A gentle 1.5 g stop from 18 m/s needs v²/(2·1.5g) = 11.0 m of travel, which can't happen at the ground. It would have to begin 11 m up, with the momentum going to the endless ocean, which the list doesn't allow. The README's alternative figures reproduce: T 1.224 s, ppv at 5 m 2.52 mm/s → 0.0013 mm/s.
The ground's elastic take at the least effort, by a 1D impedance estimate, is about 220 J (1.5% of 14.6 kJ), so 'energy taken back' holds to about 1–2% at the default.

Courtesy ceiling with the switch on: plaster at 26,930–27,050 kg-force (29.7%). shakeFrom gives 'landing'. At the ceiling the landing is 44.5 m/s, T 12.6 ms, ppv 51.1 mm/s against a 50.8 mm/s limit. Its peak push of 0.64 MN (0.95 MPa over 0.67 m²) is within the slab's 2.5 MPa, so the ceiling doesn't depend on the bearing problem.

With the switch off: the passenger hazard at 332.7/334.2 kg-force (0.37%), and the held throw goes 3.03 m. All-out: 80.82 m/s, 667.9 m, landing at 81.15 m/s; the launch at 136.6 g over 60 ms and the drag at 3.5 g no longer count with the switch on.

Below 100% absorbed, against the base branch: at 50% the ceiling was 78,150 kg-force (passenger) and now there is none. At 0% it was 39,310 (others on) and 39,650 (others off) and now there is none. With all four powers off, all-out, the person lands 213.9 m away at 34.51 m/s and plaster may crack within 1.364 m: no ceiling.

At a 10^9 kg dial with the switch on: boom and air at 1.602 million kg-force and plaster at 27,000, unchanged. Windows 1.777 million → 387.7 million (use) and houses 1.602 million → 240.7 million (use), matching the README's 388 and 241 million.

Switch off, nothing changes: the new passenger rule (!sp && (launch || drag)) equals the old one when sp is false, by code. I compared base and PR planner results (goal, every hazard, every preset, reach) in 72 cases (dials 10^5, 10^8 and 10^9.15 kg; four power sets; person with sp off, car with sp on and off; 10° and 45°): 0 differ. throwObject never reads safePassenger, so Safe passenger changes no trajectory, and no result gains a key.

passengerDrag at every share: drag × dragFactor (1 − airAbsorb) against the held 1.5 g. With the switch on the hazard never fires at 0, 0.6 or 1 (also checked by test 5a). passengerLaunch is the old launch clause. powers.js --skip-off: 155/155 pass.

The landing blast removal: for a person, 'land' = shock(vImpact, Eimpact) is the only blast source where they land. For supersonic person landings with partial absorption (90% and 99%), the air's remaining share of the drag over the last 30 m is 3.1% and 0.31% of Eimpact. So 'no blast where they land' leaves out only a small bow-shock term, and the path term near him and the boom hazard still count.

Heat on the Throw tab: with keepForm off and airAbsorb < 1, passengerText (maxStagT > 1200 K) and the effort box's hotP (relativistic, or maxStagT > 1200) never say 'unharmed'. The rule matches the 'melt or burn away' item.

Catch at the defaults: the lob at 8.35 m/s has no ride-limit flag. The 0% fastball (81 m/s, drag 3.5 g) is no longer flagged. The miss lands 48.4 m behind him at 60.3 m/s and takes back 164 kJ (= ½·90.26·60.3²). With the switch off the lob is past the ride limits ('Throw: 2.3 g'), as the README says.

Default page text matches the engine: 'Lands at 18 m/s · 14.6 kJ taken back: Safe passenger'; the ceiling text at 30% (27 t) from plaster; the credit 'Safe passenger is on, so it leaves out the person pressed past the ride limits'; and at least effort 'rattles windows … 5 m from where it lands' (2.5 mm/s at 5 m, above 1 mm/s).
The research relabel of comic_passenger_drag_g: label and note now say the speeds judge the drag with Safe passenger off. The status stays 'estimate'.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed. In the game of catch, the missed-person callout says the person comes down 'unharmed' even when the same view says their skin melts. README decision 6 says Safe passenger doesn't cover heating and that the page must not call a person unharmed where the flight would melt or burn them. The Throw tab follows that rule (passengerText's `burns` test, app.html:1330, plus a shots.js check), but the catch miss branch (app.html:3028) only tests `o.passenger && state.safePassenger`. Pull request 2's page shows no 'unharmed' claim for the same save, so this pull request introduced it. It needs two defaults off (Things keep their form, and part of Air resistance absorbed), but it is a false safety claim sitting beside a 'skin melts' chip and it breaks a stated decision, so major stands. Two related points: the Game of catch card ('if the catch is missed they come down unharmed') has no heat caveat. The 'Hits his palms' tile's '(Safe passenger: spread through them, no harm)' refers only to the g-force, so it is a lesser issue. Older and outside this pull request: the catch judges a person's heating as steel ('past the 1,538 °C where steel starts to melt'), because OBJ_MATERIAL has no entry for a person. So the catch's heat.kind would call a person 'warm' between 927 and 1,538 °C. The fix should therefore use the Throw tab's 1,200 K stagnation test, not heat.kind.

findings.title: A fast person's landing: the page says 'no crater' but sends the whole push into ground that can bear only a small fraction of it (no bearing cap, unlike Soft landing, the analogue the PR cites)
findings.location: rex-strength-lab/src/engine.js MOVES.throw.landShake (~3955) and passengerLanding (~3981); src/app.html:1631 (Impact line) and 3028 (catch miss); README decisions 4–5
findings.evidence: Engine (my script). Person at 45°, four powers on, Safe passenger on, all-out at 10^9.15 kg: lands at 10,110 m/s, J = 912,500 kg·m/s over T = 1 ms (landShake's floor), so the mean push is 9.1e8 N. The 10 cm concrete slab's qult is 2.5 MPa. Even over the person's whole 0.67 m² frontal area it bears 1.675e6 N, so the push is 545 times that. ppvNonlinear(…, 5 m) is true. The page shows 'Impact: 1.1 t TNT, all of it taken back by Safe passenger, so no crater, quake or blast where they land. The landing's push still reaches the ground and shakes it.' and the effort box shows 'Plaster may crack … now out to 247 m from where it lands'. The ground stops bearing the mean push from a landing speed of about 102 m/s (m v²/L = 161.5 v² = 1.675e6 N), which is an all-out 45° throw at a dial of about 145,000 kg; the default dial (81 m/s, mean 1.06 MN) is just under it. The engine's own precedent: for his landings with Soft landing, 'soft landing takes back the energy, not the force'. Past the bearing his feet punch in (landSink), and with Unbreakable footing the ground takes at most landBear × T, with the rest to the endless ocean (MOVES.jump.shake: canon's 'the ground's share it can't bear'). Capped the same way (J ≤ qult × 0.67 m² × T), the 10^9.15 kg landing's plaster reach is 13 m instead of 247 m (10^8 kg: 13 m vs 89 m; 10^6 kg: 16 m vs 32 m). A rough 1D impedance estimate (∫F²dt / (ρ c_p A)) also says that pushing real ground that hard would put about 47% of the landing energy into it, so 'all of it taken back' and 'the whole push reaches the ground' can't both hold. At the least effort the same estimate gives 1.5%, so the default case is fine.
findings.expected: With the energy taken back and no crater, the ground can take only what it bears; the rest is canon's listed momentum case, 'the ground's share it can't bear'. That is the rule the engine already applies to his own Soft landing with Unbreakable footing on, and the README calls this landing 'as Soft landing does'. Or, if the full push is kept, the ground gives way and 'no crater' is wrong. As it stands the page claims both.
findings.fix: In landShake (or a passenger-specific shake) with Safe passenger on, cap the ground's take at the landing site's bearing over the pulse: J ≤ max(0, qult × contact area − weight) × T, as jump's cap() does. Send the rest to the endless ocean, and add a line saying so. Or keep the full push and drop 'no crater' above the bearing speed. Either way, say in the README where the model stops (about 100 m/s on the default slab).

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced in the engine. landShake (unchanged here) sends the person's whole momentum into the ground over max(1 ms, L/v), with no bearing limit. Past a landing of about 102 m/s (an all-out 45° throw at a dial of about 145,000 kg; the default dial gives 81 m/s, ratio 0.6), the mean push is more than the 10 cm slab bears even over the person's whole 0.67 m² frontal area. At 10^9.15 kg it is 545 times that. Even so, the page says 'no crater' (the Impact line, and the catch miss callout at any speed), and the shaking reach uses the full push. The lab's own precedent says taking back the energy doesn't hold the ground. With Soft landing alone, his feet still punch in past the bearing ('soft landing takes back the energy, not the force'; app.html:1730: 'so his feet punch in, up to …'). Only Unbreakable footing caps what the ground takes and supplies the rest. Decisions 4 and 5 don't address the bearing, and nothing says where the model stops being valid (the owner's standard). The page does flag the shaking as rough ('beyond the elastic model’s range'), but not the crater claim. One caution on the proposed fix: capping and sending the excess to the endless ocean uses canon's 'the ground's share it can't bear'. Canon ties that case to Unbreakable footing under them (RT A1, A4), and the engine's own momentum list says the same (engine.js comment near 4285). Applying it to a person's landing site would be a new reading, so it needs the owners' confirmation. The 1D-impedance energy argument is rough: with the model's soil-under-slab ground (rho 2000, cs 250) I get about 40–45%, close to the reviewer's 47%, but it is an estimate, not a defect on its own.

verdict.better_fix: The fix that adds no new canon: keep the full push, but past the bearing don't claim 'no crater'. In the Impact line and the catch miss callout, when m v²/L > qult × 0.67 m², say: 'Safe passenger takes back its energy, but its push is more than the ground can bear, so it gives way where they land (the lab doesn’t size the hole).' findings.outcome: Fixed as the session lead decided (the skeptic's fix that adds no canon): the landing's momentum stays real and whole, and past what the ground bears the page no longer claims 'no crater'. src/engine.js: PASSENGER.landGround(o, v, surface) gives the landing's mean push (its momentum over landShake's own stop, max(1 ms, L / v): exactly landShake's mean push, half its Hann peak), what the ground bears (its bearing pressure over the person's whole facing area, 0.67 m², less their weight; on sand and gravel the bearing grows with that patch's width, taken as its square root, 0.82 m), gives (push > bear) and vBear (where they are equal). Found on the way and recorded in Known limits: on ice, which has no ground-wave model, nothing counts a person breaking through; at a 10^9 kg dial the courtesy ceiling (the boom, a landing at about 340 m/s) is past ice's 140 m/s. On the slab the person throw's ceiling (plaster, a landing at 44.5 m/s) stays below the bearing; at the default dial even all-out (81 m/s) does; all-out at about 145,000 kg reaches it. Reverts: bear-throw, bear-impact, bear-catch and card-bearing (page) and bear-engine (gives always false: test/powers.js 155/156, and two page checks) each fail.

findings.title: Very fast impact line says 'no … quake' while the same tab says the landing cracks plaster 247 m away
findings.evidence: Save {action:'throw', obj:'person', logKg:9.15}, effort All-out (the shots.js case). The happenings list says 'Impact: 1.1 t TNT, all of it taken back by Safe passenger, so no crater, quake or blast where they land. The landing's push still reaches the ground and shakes it.' The effort box says 'Plaster may crack at 5 m from lifting 27 t; now out to 247 m from where it lands'. RESTRAINT.reach for the same run gives plaster 246.7 m, rattle 5,062 m and feel 12,780 m. With the switch off, the old line never mentioned a quake for this landing (r.quake = 0.58, below its threshold of 2), so 'no quake' is a new claim. Even with the bearing cap above, plaster still cracks out to 13 m.
findings.expected: Shaking that cracks plaster hundreds of metres away and is felt for kilometres is what a reader calls a quake. Taking back the energy removes the energy-based magnitude (r.quake), not the momentum's shaking, which the page itself counts.
findings.fix: Drop 'quake': 'Impact: X, all of it taken back by Safe passenger, so no crater or blast where they land. The landing's push still reaches the ground and shakes it (the effort box gives how far).' Update the shots.js regex to match.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed. The new Impact line says 'no crater, quake or blast where they land', then in the next sentence that the push shakes the ground. The same tab's effort box says plaster may crack out to 247 m, and RESTRAINT.reach gives felt shaking out to 12.8 km. Safe passenger doesn't change that shaking: landShake doesn't read the switch, so with it off the page shows the same 247 m. The only thing the switch removes is r.quake, the energy-based magnitude, which is 0.58 here and was never shown (threshold 2). So 'no quake' claims a difference that doesn't exist, and it contradicts the page's own shaking figures.

findings.title: The copy says the push is spread 'as gravity is' with 'no internal stress', then that they 'feel' a manageable push. By its own physics they would feel nothing (free fall)
findings.location: rex-strength-lab/src/app.html:1320 (passengerText) and 348 (switch label); src/static-data.js 'Their powers' card
findings.evidence: Throw text: 'Safe passenger: his push is spread through their whole body in proportion to its mass, as gravity is, so at the launch they feel only a manageable push.' Card: 'his hands put no stress on them (a body pushed that way has no internal stress: Cauchy's equation of motion), and the air's drag in flight and the landing are spread through them too. They feel a manageable push throughout'. A body force proportional to mass at every point gives zero stress and, by the equivalence principle, no sensation (the otoliths are pushed too). The person feels what they would in free fall, which is what the old switch text said ('they float as if falling'). The 'so' in the Throw text is a non sequitur. It matters most at the landing: about 59 g mean (118 g peak) at the least effort, 1,200 g mean at the default all-out, and about 10^6 g at a 10 km/s landing (T floored at 1 ms), all 'felt' only as 'manageable'.
findings.expected: Canon's 'feels a manageable force' is met by zero felt force, so the page can keep canon's word without contradicting its own mechanism. It follows the brief's requested wording, but as written the physics sentence and the 'feel' sentence disagree.
findings.fix: For example: 'his push is spread through their whole body in proportion to its mass, as gravity is, so it puts no stress on them: they feel no more than a manageable push (spread perfectly, they float as if falling).' Use the same in the card and the switch.

verdict.reasoning: The texts are reproduced as quoted, but they don't contradict each other. 'They feel only a manageable push' is an upper bound, and a body force with no internal stress (felt force zero, as in free fall) meets it. So the 'so' is a valid inference: spread like gravity, no stress, so at most a manageable push. The wording is canon's own (RT 4.2: 'feels a manageable force'). The brief asked for it explicitly, to replace the old 'they float as if falling' (BRIEF-canon.md item 5, Copy: 'Say they feel a manageable push, spread through them, at the launch, in the air and when they land'). The physics sentence (no internal stress: Cauchy's equation of motion) is correct, and the page never gives a nonzero felt force. The g figures the reviewer cites (59 g mean and 119 g peak at 18 m/s; about 10⁶ g at 10 km/s) are the ground pulse's, and README decision 4 says Safe passenger spreads that push through them. Adding '(spread perfectly, they float as if falling)' would be a clarity choice, not a fix to wrong physics.
